title: C6: invariance under algebraically closed extension
statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated connected curve over $k$, and let
$r$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Then the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_r$ satisfies $\mathcal C_6(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]: the pullback maps
$\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of [def-sc-field-extension] are
isomorphisms for every $q\geq0$.

proof.text: The quotient constant sheaf is killed by r, as proved by nsmul_id_constantModSheaf. This remains true after pullback along the identity. Forgetting module coefficients preserves the annihilation equation, checked directly on each section.

For the standard projection after an algebraically closed extension, apply the prime-injective-acyclicity comparison. Its degree-zero hypothesis is isIso_globalSectionsUpperStarMap_algClosed_extension and its positive-degree acyclicity hypothesis is subsingleton_cohomology_upperStar_injective_algClosed_extension. This proves comparison for every module sheaf killed by r, without a finiteness assumption on coefficients.

Present the arbitrary morphism Spec k′ → Spec k as Spec.map a using Spec.map_surjective and put the corresponding algebra structure on k′. Use h.isoPullback.inv to compare the given square with the standard pullback. Apply the cohomology restriction-square transport with identity on C and that isomorphism on the base change; both vertical cohomology restrictions are bijective by topological invariance. The resulting two equivalences and the commuting equation transport injectivity and surjectivity of the standard comparison to the exact map in C6.
